$BTC 2-Year MA Multiplier is signaling that Bitcoin is in its value area.

All this does is see if Bitcoin trades below its 2 year moving average. Everything underneath, marked in green, is usually considered good long term value. It marked the bottom in every cycle so far, but as you can see with a big note. Last cycle it traded down there for almost 1.5 years and extended up to -30% deeper.

So take it with a big grain of salt.

But we can all agree that these valuations make more sense than if price were to be trading near its 2 year moving average x5 (red line) which has roughly marked the top in every cycle except the last one.

Choppy days are where most bad trades get made, not trending ones.

When nothing is actually moving, the temptation is to find a setup just to stay busy. That's usually how you end up trading against yourself.

You will end up in several losses in a week and in the end prices did not move an inch. That's when you know your strategy or trading style is not working in that specific environment.

Altcoins in a bear market aren't cheap just because they're down 80%.

Down 80% can always become down 95%. Down 95% can become down 99% etc.

Valuation only matters when the market decides it does.

And the one thing that has been very clear is that FDV (Fully Diluted Valuation) is the price you really pay.

Plenty of big VC coins are down over 95% price wise from their highs but might "only" be down about 50% in their market cap based on circulating supply.

Token unlocks and inflation are your biggest enemy when bullish momentum and buyers dry up. They will make the difference between alts being down -80% or -99% by the end of a bear market.

Every cycle has a moment where it feels like it's over and most people give up.

Those moments have never actually been the end, and I doubt they ever will. 

It's just the part that separates who stays in this long term and who doesn't.
